backlog.spec: Append the full RDKit 2D descriptor set (rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList, roughly 200 values such as MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD/HBA counts, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring counts) to the Morgan bit vector for each molecule. Replace NaN and infinite values with 0 and clip extreme values to the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles of the training set. Keep the random forest otherwise unchanged. Descriptors such as Crippen logP and TPSA carry lipophilicity signal that bit fingerprints capture only indirectly, so they should help on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the binary Morgan bit vector with the hashed count vector from rdFingerprintGenerator (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) at radius 2 with 2048 bits. Counts keep information about repeated substructures, such as several halogens or amide groups, which the bit vector collapses. Leave the random forest and its settings unchanged so the effect of the representation is isolated.
backlog.title: Morgan count fingerprints instead of bits

backlog.spec: logD depends on ionization at pH 7.4, which Morgan bits represent poorly. Add a small set of counts computed with RDKit SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, phenols, aliphatic amines (primary, secondary, tertiary, excluding amides), amidines, and quaternary nitrogens. Include the number of ionizable groups of each class as extra features, appended to the existing fingerprint. Keep the random forest unchanged.
backlog.title: Ionization-state descriptors for pH-dependent logD

backlog.spec: Swap the random forest for a LightGBM regressor with objective='l1', which optimises the mean absolute error the harness scores. Use the same Morgan bit features. Set num_leaves around 31, learning_rate 0.05, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, and about 600 boosting rounds. Set n_jobs=8 and pass random_state=seed. Gradient boosting with an absolute loss often beats random forests on regression targets like logD.
backlog.title: LightGBM with L1 objective on the same features

backlog.spec: Train both the existing random forest and a LightGBM regressor (objective='l1' or 'huber') on the same Morgan features, each with the seed passed through. Return the average of their test predictions, with weights 0.5 and 0.5. Two model families with different error patterns usually reduce variance on out-of-scaffold molecules, so the blend should beat either model alone. Keep the blend simple with no stacking.
backlog.title: Blend random forest with a gradient-boosted model

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix between binary Morgan fingerprints of training and test molecules, K = sum(min)/sum(max) on the bit vectors, and fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed', epsilon around 0.1, and C tuned over {1, 10} using the training set only. Chemical-similarity kernels are a strong baseline for small-molecule property prediction. Return the SVR predictions. Keep the code short, using numpy broadcasting for the similarity matrix.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Keep the random forest but regularise it for unseen scaffolds: set min_samples_leaf to 3 or 5 and max_features to 0.15 instead of 0.3, and set max_samples=0.7 so each tree sees a bootstrap subset. These changes trade a little training fit for smoother predictions on new chemotypes. Sweep these two values over a small grid inside fit_predict using an inner 3-fold split on the training data, then refit on all of it.
backlog.title: Shrink random forest leaves and feature subsampling

backlog.spec: Before fitting, drop Morgan bits that are set in fewer than 1 percent or more than 99 percent of training molecules, using the training set only so there is no leakage. Apply the same column mask to the test features. Dropping uninformative columns reduces noise in the random forest's feature sampling, which can help a model with max_features=0.3 choose more useful splits. Keep all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='l1' on Morgan features plus RDKit descriptors. Carve out 10 percent of the training molecules as an inner validation set, grouped by Murcko scaffold, to choose the number of boosting rounds with early stopping (patience 50, up to 2000 rounds) and a learning-rate schedule that decays from 0.05. Refit on the full training data with the chosen round count, scaled up by about 10 percent. Early stopping avoids both underfitting and overfitting without relying on a fixed round count.
backlog.title: Early-stopped boosting with inner validation

backlog.spec: The harness scores mean absolute error, so the median is a better central estimate than the mean for skewed prediction spreads. Keep the random forest, but instead of calling model.predict, collect the per-tree predictions from model.estimators_ (each estimator's predict on the test features), and return the element-wise median across trees. This needs no retraining and costs only a little extra inference time. It may reduce the effect of outlier trees on molecules far from the training set.
backlog.title: Predict the median of tree outputs instead of the mean

backlog.spec: Keep the Tanimoto precomputed-kernel SVR. Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 3 inner folds using a RandomState seeded by the seed argument (group by Murcko scaffold if easy, otherwise plain KFold with shuffle). For each (C, epsilon) in a small grid, e.g. C in {1, 3, 10, 30} and epsilon in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}, fit SVR on the inner-train kernel submatrix and score mean absolute error on the inner-validation part. Refit SVR on all training data with the best (C, epsilon) and return its test predictions. Precompute the full train and test kernels once and slice them, so the grid stays cheap.
backlog.title: Inner-CV grid search over SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR with sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed'). Center the training targets by subtracting their mean before fitting and add the mean back to the predictions. Choose alpha from {0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by a 3-fold inner split over the training molecules, using the seed argument for the shuffle. Refit on all training data with the best alpha and return the predictions for the test molecules. Everything else (Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits, Tanimoto formula) stays the same.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge regression on the Tanimoto kernel instead of SVR

backlog.spec: Keep the SVR and the Tanimoto similarity matrices, but transform each kernel entry before fitting: K' = K ** p (elementwise), with p chosen from {0.5, 1, 2, 3} by a single inner holdout (about 20% of the training molecules, split by the seed argument). Sharper kernels (p > 1) emphasize near neighbours and flatter ones (p < 1) smooth across the set. Refit with the chosen p on all training data and predict the test molecules. Clip the kernel to [0, 1] first so the power is well defined.
backlog.title: Exponentiated Tanimoto kernel with a power parameter

backlog.spec: Build two binary fingerprints per molecule: Morgan radius 2 with 2048 bits (as now) and RDKit atom-pair fingerprint with 2048 bits from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator. Compute the Tanimoto kernel for each (train-train and test-train). Use the average of the two kernels as the single precomputed kernel for the SVR. Keep C and epsilon unchanged. Both fingerprints are computed with RDKit only, so no new packages are needed.
backlog.title: Averaged ECFP4 and atom-pair Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Before fitting the SVR, clip the training targets to the 1st and 99th percentiles of train_y (computed inside fit_predict on the training fold only). Fit on the clipped values and predict the test molecules as usual. The goal is to limit the influence of a few extreme logD measurements on the epsilon-insensitive loss. Do not clip the test predictions. Keep the kernel, C, and epsilon unchanged.
backlog.title: Winsorize training targets before fitting

backlog.spec: Train K=7 SVRs with the same Tanimoto kernel, each on a bootstrap resample (sample with replacement, same size as the training set) of the training molecules. Draw the resample indices from np.random.RandomState(seed + k) for member k, so every run is reproducible from the seed argument. Predict the test molecules with each member and return the median of the K predictions per molecule (the median fits the MAE metric). Subset the precomputed kernel with the resample indices instead of recomputing it.
backlog.title: Bagged ensemble of SVRs on bootstrap resamples

backlog.spec: Replace SVR(kernel='precomputed') with NuSVR(kernel='precomputed', C=C, nu=nu). Choose nu from {0.3, 0.5, 0.7} by a 3-fold inner split of the training molecules, with the split driven by the seed argument, and score by MAE on the held-out inner part. Refit on all training data with the best nu and predict the test molecules. NuSVR controls the fraction of support vectors instead of the epsilon tube width, so this is a different regularization path over the same kernel.
backlog.title: NuSVR with the nu parameter tuned

backlog.spec: Compute the SVR predictions as now. Also compute a kNN prediction for each test molecule: take its k=10 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity (from the same kernel matrix) and average their training targets weighted by the similarity raised to the power 3. Return 0.8 times the SVR prediction plus 0.2 times the kNN prediction. The weights are fixed, so no extra tuning is needed. The kNN term adds a local, memory-style correction that the kernel SVR can smooth away.
backlog.title: Blend the SVR with a similarity-weighted kNN regressor

backlog.spec: Run a 3-fold inner split of the training molecules, with the split driven by the seed argument. Fit the SVR on two inner folds and predict the third, and collect out-of-fold predictions for all training molecules. Fit a simple linear map y = a * pred + b on those out-of-fold predictions, using least absolute deviation (or ordinary least squares if that is simpler). Then fit the SVR on all training data, apply the linear map to its test predictions, and return the result. The map corrects the typical shrinkage of kernel regressors toward the mean.
backlog.title: Post-hoc linear recalibration from inner out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Change the Morgan fingerprint to radius 3 (ECFP6-like) with useChirality=True, still 2048 bits, using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator. Keep the Tanimoto kernel and SVR settings unchanged. Stereochemistry and the larger neighbourhood give the kernel more discriminative power for ionizable and stereo-dependent logD series. Molecules with no stereocentres are unaffected by the chirality flag, so the only effect is on the stereo-containing molecules and the larger radius.
backlog.title: Chirality-aware ECFP6 fingerprints for the kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the single ECFP4 kernel with a sum of Tanimoto kernels over unhashed Morgan fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 (use a larger fpSize, e.g. 4096, or GetSparseCountFingerprint-style bit sets). Build each Tanimoto matrix with the existing get_tanimoto function, then average them: K = (K1 + K2 + K3) / 3 for both train-train and test-train. Feed the averaged kernel to the same SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=10, epsilon=0.1). Keep C and epsilon unchanged so the only change is the kernel. Memory is fine at this size.
backlog.title: Multi-radius summed Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute a small descriptor vector per molecule with RDKit: Crippen MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, MolWt, HBD and HBA count, and formal charge count. Standardize them using training-set mean and std only. Build an RBF kernel on these descriptors, K_d(x,y) = exp(-gamma * ||x-y||^2) with gamma = 1/(num_features) set on the training data. Combine with the Tanimoto kernel as K = K_tan + 0.5 * K_d for train-train and test-train alike, then fit the same SVR with precomputed kernel. The combined kernel is still positive semidefinite since it is a sum of PSD kernels. This injects a logP-like prior the fingerprint kernel cannot express directly.
backlog.title: Physchem RBF kernel added to Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Augment the training set before fitting. For each training molecule, create two extra copies whose fingerprint bits are randomly zeroed with probability 0.15, using np.random.RandomState(seed) so the seed argument controls all randomness. Stack the original and augmented rows, duplicate the targets accordingly, and build the Tanimoto kernel on the augmented set. Fit SVR with the same C and epsilon, but raise C modestly if needed to keep the effective regularization similar. Predict on the clean test fingerprints. The intent is to smooth the decision function across near-neighbour bit patterns and reduce overfitting to specific substructure bits.
backlog.title: Fingerprint-bit dropout augmentation

backlog.spec: Fit the current SVR once on all training data. Compute absolute residuals on the training set using the in-sample predictions. Drop the 5 percent of training molecules with the largest residuals, then refit the SVR on the remaining 95 percent with the same kernel, C and epsilon, and predict the test set with the refit model. This is a single deterministic trimming step with no extra hyperparameter search, and it targets measurement-noise outliers in logD labels that a MAE objective is still sensitive to through the support vectors.
backlog.title: Trimmed refit to drop label outliers

backlog.spec: Compute, for each training molecule, its local density as the mean Tanimoto similarity to its k=10 nearest training neighbours, excluding itself. Set sample weight w_i = 1 / (density_i + 0.05), normalize weights to mean 1, and pass them as sample_weight to model.fit on the precomputed kernel. This down-weights molecules in crowded chemical clusters, which otherwise dominate the fit, and up-weights isolated scaffolds, which matter for the scaffold-split test folds. Keep C and epsilon fixed.
backlog.title: Density-based sample weights for SVR

backlog.spec: Before fitting, transform the training targets by a rank-based Gaussian quantile map: rank each training y, convert the rank to a quantile in (0,1) using (rank - 0.5)/n, then apply the inverse normal CDF using scipy.stats.norm.ppf. Fit the SVR on these transformed targets with the same kernel. At prediction time, map the SVR outputs back to the original scale by interpolating the sorted transformed training targets against the sorted original training targets (np.interp). This makes the target distribution closer to Gaussian, so the fixed epsilon tube covers a more uniform share of points, and the back-transform keeps predictions on the logD scale.
backlog.title: Quantile-normalized target with inverse transform

backlog.spec: Avoid any nested search. Fit SVR models on the precomputed Tanimoto kernel for every pair in the fixed grid C in {1, 3, 10, 30} and epsilon in {0.05, 0.2}, which is 8 models in total. Each model is cheap because the kernel is shared, so compute K_train and K_test once and reuse them. Return the unweighted mean of the 8 predictions. Averaging over a modest hyperparameter spread reduces sensitivity to a single C choice and should give a steadier MAE across the 15 folds without the crash risk of the earlier nested grid search.
backlog.title: Averaged SVR over a fixed C and epsilon grid

backlog.spec: Train a sequence of three SVRs on the same precomputed Tanimoto kernel. Stage 1 uses epsilon=0.5 and fits the raw targets. Stage k for k=2 and 3 fits a new SVR with epsilon set to 0.3 and then 0.1 on the residual target y minus the cumulative prediction of earlier stages, where in-sample predictions are used for residuals. The final prediction on test molecules is the sum of all stage predictions evaluated on the test kernel. Keep C=10. This is a coarse-to-fine schedule that first captures the broad trend with a wide tube and then refines the tighter structure, similar to boosting with a kernel base learner.
backlog.title: Cascade of SVRs with shrinking epsilon

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR with a small neural network for a bold alternative. Use sklearn MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), activation='relu', alpha=1e-2 for L2 weight decay, learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=300 with early_stopping=True and validation_fraction=0.1, and a seed derived from the seed argument. Train 5 members with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 on the binary Morgan fingerprints and average their predictions on the test set. Scale the targets to zero mean and unit variance before fitting and invert afterwards. Keep the total runtime under the per-job budget by limiting the ensemble to 5 members.
backlog.title: Multi-layer perceptron ensemble on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Keep the Tanimoto SVR as the base model. To avoid leakage from in-sample residuals, compute out-of-fold SVR predictions on the training set with a 5-fold KFold split seeded by the seed argument, using the precomputed kernel sub-blocks. Form residuals r = y - oof_pred. Fit a LightGBM regressor with objective='l1', n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15 and min_child_samples=20 on RDKit descriptors (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, ring count, aromatic ring count, fraction sp3) to predict r. For test molecules, the final prediction is the full-data SVR prediction plus the LightGBM residual prediction. The base model captures fingerprint similarity while the descriptor booster corrects systematic physicochemical trends that the bit kernel misses.
backlog.title: Residual boosting on physchem descriptors atop the SVR

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute MACCS keys for every molecule with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a float32 numpy array (167 bits). Build a Tanimoto kernel for train-train and test-train with the existing get_tanimoto helper. Add it to the running sum of kernels so the final kernel is the mean of three matrices (Morgan radius 2, atom pair, MACCS). Divide K_train and K_test by 3.0 instead of 2.0. Leave the SVR, its C and epsilon, and the rest of the script unchanged.
backlog.title: Add MACCS Tanimoto kernel to the kernel average

backlog.spec: Compute topological torsion fingerprints with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048) for all train and test molecules, as float32 numpy arrays. Compute the Tanimoto kernel train-train and test-train with get_tanimoto. Add it to K_train and K_test alongside the Morgan and atom-pair kernels, then divide both by 3.0 so the result is the mean of three kernels. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Add topological torsion Tanimoto kernel to the average

backlog.spec: Build a feature-invariant Morgan generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Use it to produce float32 fingerprints for train and test. Compute the Tanimoto kernel train-train and test-train, add it to the existing Morgan and atom-pair kernel sum, and divide by 3.0 so the final kernel is the mean of three. No other changes.
backlog.title: Add feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP) Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the Tanimoto kernel on the Morgan bit vector with a MinMax kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits, generator.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). For two count vectors a and b, K(a,b) = sum_j min(a_j, b_j) / sum_j max(a_j, b_j). Compute it with a loop over train rows in numpy (vectorize per row using np.minimum and np.maximum), giving train-train and test-train matrices. Keep the atom-pair Tanimoto kernel and the averaging over two kernels. Keep the SVR settings.
backlog.title: MinMax kernel on count Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Before fitting the SVR, subtract the mean of train_y from the target and store it as y_mean. Fit SVR on the centered target (train_y minus y_mean). At prediction time, add y_mean back to the SVR output on test_smiles. Apply the same centering to the training residual fit that the script does, so the offset is consistent. Keep the kernel and C and epsilon unchanged. This makes the SVR epsilon-tube and C act on deviations from the mean instead of on the raw logD offset.
backlog.title: Mean-center the training target before SVR

backlog.spec: After computing the final test_preds array, clip it to the interval [min(train_y), max(train_y)] using np.clip. This removes extreme extrapolations from the kernel model on test molecules with unusual scaffolds. Do not change training. Return the clipped array.
backlog.title: Clip predictions to the training target range

backlog.spec: Remove the LightGBM residual model entirely. Keep the Tanimoto-kernel SVR on the averaged Morgan and atom-pair kernels as the sole predictor. In fit_predict, delete the 80/20 split block, the train_lm and train_lm_full boosters, and the get_descriptors calls, and return the SVR prediction on K_test directly. This ablation measures whether the in-sample residual booster helps or hurts, and it simplifies the script.
backlog.title: Ablate the descriptor residual booster

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform average of the Morgan (radius 2) and atom-pair Tanimoto kernels with a weighted sum: 0.5 times Morgan plus 0.5 times atom pair, but first add a torsion kernel with weight 0.25 and scale the Morgan and atom-pair weights to 0.375 each, so total weight is 1. Compute the three Tanimoto kernels as float32 matrices, combine them with those weights, and then fit the SVR on the combined matrix. Only the weighting changes; no grid search is run at fit time.
backlog.title: Fixed-grid weighting of the three kernels

backlog.spec: Change the atom-pair fingerprint to fpSize=8192 and use count fingerprints via GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the atom-pair generator. Compute the Tanimoto kernel on these count vectors using get_tanimoto, with the same train and test matrices. Keep Morgan bit fingerprints and the average over two kernels. Keep the SVR settings unchanged. Check the memory budget: 8192 float32 columns for about 3000 molecules is roughly 100 MB, which is acceptable.
backlog.title: Atom-pair kernel with larger hashed size and counts

backlog.spec: Compute Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints with rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory and rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Generate.Gen2DFingerprint, converting each result to a numpy float32 bit vector of fixed length. Because the feature factory is slow, skip any molecule that fails and use a zero vector. Build a Tanimoto kernel train-train and test-train from these vectors, add it to the Morgan and atom-pair kernel sum, and divide by 3.0. Keep the SVR settings unchanged. If runtime exceeds the budget, drop this idea.
backlog.title: Pharmacophore 2D (Gobbi) fingerprint kernel

incumbent.description: Implement an averaged Tanimoto kernel using both Morgan (radius 2) and RDKit atom-pair fingerprints.

memo:
Helped: changing the model family and kernel. The SVR on a Tanimoto kernel (slot 7) scored 0.6489, down 0.0742 from baseline. Averaging Tanimoto kernels over several fingerprints helped again. Slot 20 scored 0.6042. Slot 24 scored 0.5925/0.5961 (two runs). The incumbent, slot 31, averages Morgan and atom-pair kernels and scored 0.5683, down 0.0259.

Did not help: kNN blend (+0.0021), count fingerprints (+0.0000), sample weights (+0.0002), an SVR grid ensemble (+0.0060) and dropping rare/common bits (0.5680, within noise). RF/LightGBM blends and recalibration were clearly worse.

Waste: many patch failures and crashes, mostly from descriptor imports and nested search.

Next: add more diverse fingerprint kernels, such as other radii, topological torsion or MACCS, to the averaged kernel. Try kernel ridge or a GP on the same kernel. Make each SEARCH block short and exact.
